newsitem.title: USA: Micron seeks expanded dumping probe.
newsitem.headline: Micron seeks expanded dumping probe.

text.p: Micron Technology Inc. said Thursday it asked the U.S. Commerce Department to expand its investigation of alleged dumping by Korean semiconductor makers Hyundai Electronics Industries and LG Semicon.
The department is currently reviewing U.S. imports of Hyundai and LG Semicon chips from May 1, 1995 through April 30, 1996, Micron said.
Boise, Idaho-based Micron said it is asking the department to investigate activity by the companies during the period between May and August 1996.
Hyundai Electronics is a unit of Hyundai Group. LG Semicon is a unit of LG Group.

"The DRAM industry has witnessed a severe decline in prices since the beginning of the year," said Steve Appleton, chairman, chief executive officer and president of Micron. DRAMs are dynamic random access memory chips used in computers.
"Today we are asking the Department of Commerce to review this most recent period of dumping and to adjust the duty rate to reflect dumping by these two companies," Appleton said.
"Decisive action taken by the Department of Commerce and the imposing of adjusted duties will send the message to manufacturers that dumping will not be tolerated."
Micron's stock rose $1.50 to $27 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly before midday.
